symptom: `mxcli diff-local -p App/App.mpr` run from outside the project's git repository failed with `Error: failed to find changed files: failed to git diff: exit status 1`; run from a subdirectory of the repo it warned `failed to read current file App/mprcontents/…` and reported `0 modified`
cause: findChangedMxunitFiles and the `git show` calls used execCommand with no Dir, so git ran in the process's working directory; `git diff --name-status` reports paths relative to the repo root, which readFile and `git show rev:path` then resolved against the wrong directory
insight: Two separate wrong directories hide behind one 'works for me': the cwd git runs in, and the base the reported paths are relative to. Both only coincide when cwd is the repo root and the project sits at it, which is how every earlier repro ran. Run git with Dir = the project directory, ask for `--relative` paths, and read revisions as `rev:./path` — './' makes git resolve against the working directory instead of the root, so a project below the root needs no rev-parse. Test it with a real temp repo and t.Chdir to both an unrelated dir and a subdirectory; the execCommand stubs cannot see a wrong Dir.
